// AC14's needle-liveness control (issue #477). Not compiled, not a test
// target: it is parsed by the AC14 scanner and by nothing else.
//
// One raw clock read per needle, each under its own column-0 `fn` whose
// name is NOT in the scanner's permitted set — so a correct scan reports
// exactly three occurrences, one per needle, all classified as
// violations. If the scanner is blind to a needle (a mistyped spelling,
// a lost visitor arm) this file is what says so, because the domain file
// itself has no violation to see.

fn probe_a() {
    let _ = std::time::SystemTime::now();
}

fn probe_b() {
    let _ = std::time::Instant::now();
}

fn probe_c() {
    let _ = chrono::Utc::now();
}
